problems: E22 supports E2F1 occupancy at the variant in U-87 MG, but the 52-bp summit offset and ChIP peak do not show that alt has greater occupancy than ref.

E23 reports an ETS1 peak containing the variant in 786-O, contradicting H2's unqualified statement that the reported peak is elsewhere. It reports no ETS1 peak in the matching U-87 MG context; that absence is not a tested negative.

E24 supplies an ETS1 own-model prediction, aligned with E11 in predicting greater alt binding. This strengthens the binding prediction but does not demonstrate allele-specific occupancy or regulatory function.
For all chains, promoter overlap makes TERT plausible, but the cited evidence does not demonstrate that the cCRE regulates TERT or that any allele-dependent effect changes disease risk.
